⛰️ Learning

Gradient descent

In simple words

A way to train a model by changing its parameters, step by step, in the direction that makes the loss smaller.

The most common way to train a model. It works out in which direction each parameter should change to make the loss a little smaller, takes a small step that way, and repeats this thousands of times.

Example. Imagine walking down a hill in thick fog. You can't see the valley, but you can feel which way the ground slopes. Step by step downhill, you get lower and lower. The gradient is that slope.

Related words

  • Loss functionA score that measures how wrong a model's answers are; training tries to make it as small as possible.
  • Learning rateA setting that controls how big a step a model takes each time it adjusts its parameters during training.
  • BackpropagationThe method a neural network uses to work out how much each weight was to blame for a mistake.
  • Evolutionary algorithmA way of solving problems that copies evolution: the best of many tries are kept, mixed and slightly changed, generation after generation.
